To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the muon densities of extensive air showers are well described by a simple scaling model with a « normal » composition, but the simple scaling model with an « abnormal » composition does not fit the data.

(a) the muon density in extensive air showers increases with energy as a power-law with a spectral index close to 1.2, (b) the muon energy threshold for this increase is about 50 GeV and is independent of the primary energy, and (c) the muon lateral distribution function (MLDF) in the range from 100 to 200 m from the shower axis is well described by a simple power-law with a slope close to -2.0

we have measured the muon density in the energy region 5·1014 to 5·1016 eV and found it to be in good agreement with the predictions of a «normal» composition CKP-type model, with the exception of the muon densities above 200 Ge V.
